values.description: A dense talking-head Short where something changes on screen every one to two seconds.

music.notes: A driving electronic or hip-hop bed, 20 dB under the voice [MON, RES]; it comes up hard in any gap without words.

look.about: Punchy - saturated and a little contrasty, so it reads as loud as it sounds.

values.summary: Maximum energy - a zoom, pop-up, sound or layout change every couple of seconds, and fast captions.

thing_pop.about: Every concrete thing named pops up as a die-cut sticker beside the speaker, with a pop.

rules.when: Every thing you could picture (a tool, a part, a product, a price tag, an animal). Emoji or the person's own picture; never a company logo they didn't give you.

word_slam.about: The stressed word slams in big and tilted above the captions.

rules.when: The one word a sentence leans on ("NEVER", "FREE", "BROKEN"). One per sentence at most.

number_pop.about: Numbers and prices as big cyan numerals, with a ding (a till for money).

rules.when: Every number that matters, written as numerals ($12, 2 tabs, 3 hrs). Money gets sfx cash.

punch_in.about: A snap push-in that holds to the next cut (118%, the top of the sharp range [MON]).

rules.when: Every second cut or so, alternating with no punch, so the framing keeps changing; on the stressed word.

zoom_bump.about: A quick in-and-out bump (0.3 s) on a beat or a word, with a click.

rules.when: Inside a long take where nothing else changes; on a list item or a number.

shake_hit.about: A hard shake with an impact.

rules.when: A real surprise, a fail, the punchline's last word.

glitch_hit.about: A short digital glitch on a cut, with its crackle.

rules.when: A jump to a new topic, a "wait, what?" moment. Not two in a row.

flash_cut.about: A white flash over a cut (0.15 s), with a whoosh.

rules.when: A new section, the first look at a result. Never more than three flashes a second [RES].

whoosh_cut.about: A whoosh landing on a cut.

rules.when: Cuts between ideas that have no other effect.

split_broll.about: The thing being described fills the bottom half while the speaker stays in the top half (a split layout).

rules.when: There is footage of the exact thing said and the speaker's face sits in the top half. Starts within 1.5 s of the word, 4 s at most [MON]. Use the half for the thing, never a random shot.

cutaway.about: A full-frame cutaway of the thing being said, 1-2 s.

rules.when: Short punches of the exact thing; the voice carries on underneath.

riser_reveal.about: A riser that builds into a reveal (it ends on the moment).

rules.when: The build right before the payoff or the result; the music can dip under it.

bass_drop.about: A sub hit on the payoff word.

rules.when: The first frame of the hook and the payoff, under the word, never over it.

reaction_sticker.about: A reaction sticker (an emoji or a short word like "WAIT" or "OOPS") with a cartoon sound.

rules.when: A fail, a surprise, a question to the viewer, a joke landing.

crowd_laugh.about: A short audience laugh under a joke that lands.

rules.when: A real joke or a self-own that got a smile; starts after the last word, never under it.

fail_sting.about: A sad-trombone sting on a real fail.

rules.when: Something really went wrong on camera (it broke, it didn't fit); never on a success, never twice.

place_tag.about: A place tag when a place is named.

fx.rhythm: Something changes every 1-2 s (a zoom, a pop-up, a word, a sound, a layout); the payoff gets a beat of quiet.

hook.rules: Frame 0 is already moving - mid-sentence, a sticker or a word already on screen, a sub hit under it. The hook text says the promise in five words or fewer [JH]; hook and the "here's what's coming" line done by ~3 s.

sources.used_for: baseline change rate (about 4 s), punch-in range, b-roll length, music level

sources.used_for: caption look (1-3 words, ALL CAPS, one highlighted word, green alternative)
